vocabulary.meaning_en: to have no more of something
vocabulary.example: We ran out of coffee this morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to lift something; to collect someone and take them in a car; to answer the phone
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يلتقط / يُقِلّ شخصًا بالسيارة / يرد على الهاتف
vocabulary.example: Josh will pick me up at eight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to arrive (often at an expected place or time)
vocabulary.example: What time did you show up for work?
Sorry, I can't come tonight. Something came up.
I'm going to head out now. See you tomorrow.
What time will you get back from the gym?

vocabulary.meaning_en: the ability to speak a language easily and naturally
vocabulary.example: Using words in real life builds fluency.
An unexpected problem came up at work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the situation in which something happens
vocabulary.example: Learn words in context, not from lists.

fine_lines.title: head out vs get back
fine_lines.explanation_ar: head out = تغادر المكان. get back = تعود إليه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Head out = leave. Get back = return.

examples.sentence: I'll head out for lunch at 12:30.

fine_lines.title: look for vs find
fine_lines.explanation_ar: look for = تبحث (لم تجد بعد). find = تجد.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Look for = try to find (not yet). Find = get it after looking.

examples.sentence: I found it on the sofa.

expressions.phrase: I'm here to pick you up.
expressions.meaning_en: I came to take you in my car.
expressions.example: It's eight o'clock. I'm here to pick you up.
Sorry, I can't make lunch. Something came up at work.

expressions.phrase: I'll catch you when you head out.
expressions.meaning_en: I'll meet you when you leave.
expressions.example: No problem. I'll catch you when you head out.
Sorry, I can't make it today.

grammar.title: Learn phrasal verbs around your day
grammar.explanation_ar: لا تحفظ القوائم فقط؛ اربط كل فعل مركب بوقت وموقف من يومك: صباحًا run out of / look for، ثم pick up / show up، ظهرًا come up، مساءً head out / get back. فكّر في الموقف ثم اختر الإنجليزية المناسبة.
grammar.explanation_en: Don't just memorize lists. Connect each phrasal verb to a time and situation in your day: morning (run out of, look for), then pick up / show up, noon (come up), evening (head out, get back).
examples: 7 a.m.: We ran out of coffee.
9 a.m.: I showed up for work on time.
5 p.m.: I'm heading out. I'll get back at 7.

questions.question: 7 a.m., no coffee at home. You say: "We ___ coffee."
questions.explanation_en: Run out of = have no more.

questions.question: You can't go to lunch because the boss gave you work. "Sorry, something ___."
"Guys, I'm going to ___ now. See you tomorrow." (leave)
"I can't find my keys. I need to ___ them."
"Josh will ___ me ___ at 8 and drive me to work."
"What time will you ___ from the gym?" (return)
James says the best way to learn phrasal verbs is to ___.
choices: connect them to situations in your day
questions.explanation_en: Connect them to your daily situations.

questions.question: Which one can also mean "answer the phone"?
questions.explanation_ar: pick up the phone = يرد على الهاتف.
questions.explanation_en: Pick up the phone = answer it.

questions.question: "We've run out of time" means:
choices: We have a lot of time.
